title: Exquisite Cinema
review:
I can honestly say that Frank Darabont's "The Shawshank Redemption" is my favourite film of all time. It is simply perfect and it is criminal in my opinion that it missed out on so many Academy Awards in 1994.

Inspired direction from Mr. Darabont is complimented by superb performances from every member of the cast, which includes Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, Bob Gunton, William Sadler and the menacing Clancy Brown.

Based upon a Stephen King novel, "The Shawshank Redemption" is the story of banker Andy DuFresne, imprisoned for the alleged murder of his wife and her lover. As life in prison begins to take it's toll, DuFresne (Robbins) befriends prison "fixer" Red (Freeman) who is understood to be 'a man who knows how to get things'. In truth, there isn't really a definitive storyline, the film merely chronicles the trials and tribulations experienced by DuFresne over his life imprisonment, during which time he becomes a financial advisor to the prison guards and makes friends in high places, although the Warden Norton (Gunton) has other plans for his talents.

A dynamic twist in the tale is the perfect finale to this exceptional film of which there is not a bad word to be said. The 2 hrs 17 mins simply flies by and by the end this magnificent story of courage, friendship, loyalty and ultimately hope will leave you feeling warm, extremely satisfied and ready for another viewing. A beautiful movie.

title: An excellent piece of story telling!
review: On the surface level, the subject is run-of-the-mill, i.e. the torture meted out to some prison inmates. But it is the way this subject is handled, that's what makes this movie so unique and memorable. Andy Dufresne is the very heart and soul of the movie. It is the greatness, the uniqueness of his character that sets him apart from the other inmates, not to mention the fact that he is wrongly convicted. Tim Robbins is absolutely brilliant in his role. I believe this is what is supposed to mean an Academy Award winning performance. I have only seen him in another movie , 'Jacob's Ladder', which is one of the most bleak movies I have ever seen. 'Shawshank' has its bleak moments, scenes of violence and torture, but what saves them from being a little too much for viewing is the narration by Morgan Freeman's character. Two scenes, one in which Andy gets beat by some other prison inmates and the one which Tommy(Gil Bellows) is shot are, I think the most violent in the movie. But the violence is kept under control by Red's ensuing narration. It is that which also gives the movie an aura that this is the story of one man who, with his friendship with Andy, realizes that he still has life beyond the four walls of the prison and being a convict doesn't mean that he is bereft of human dignity. Morgan Freeman, as always, is perfect in his role. This is perhaps the best movie of Freeman's (except maybe 'Driving Miss Daisy'). The supporting cast is equally good, especially Gil Bellows, who gives a short but poignant performance. Good cinematography(sweeping images) and a good music score(especially the concerto Andy broadcasts across the entire prison) are some of the magical moments of the movie and what adds to its greatness. Worth every moment!

title: MOST UNDER APPRECIATED FILM EVER
review:
This film's high ranking on IMDB is both a testimony to its greatness and a spotlight on how embarrassingly out of touch the Oscar Academy is.

Congratulations to all of those involved in making one of the truly greatest films of all time.

title: My #1
review:
Low budget, weak at the box office, winless at the Academy Awards, and often considered a weak and clitched film. It's too bad that the greatest film ever made is also the most underrated.

The Shawshank Redemption is the story of Ellis Redding (Red), and his views on life, society, and an inmate named Andy Dufresne.

The story is flawless, the score is memorable, the cinematography is splendid, and the movie flows at a smooth pace all the way through its three hour length. While it often appears to be a weak film at first glance, it really just requires multiple viewings. After several viewings, anyone can begin to realize its greatness.

While movie critics can keep calling Citizen Kane the greatest, I realize it doesn't come close to so much as comparing to Shawshank. Citizen Kane doesn't let its viewers relate to its character, think his every thought, walk his every step, or breathe his every breath. Citizen Kane is a puzzling and riveting masterpiece, but like most "greats", it doesn't compare to The Shawshank Redemption.

The Shawshank Redemption is leagues away from any film I've ever seen in terms of greatness. It is timeless, memorable, original, and ultimately the best film I probably will ever see.

title: Best movie of all time!!
review: This movie has to be the most electrifing movies of all time.  This short story (originally written by Stephen King) gives a heart pounding reality of an innocent banker who uses hope, courage, and brains to OUTsmart the pison walls of Shawshank.    Morgan Freeman plays an exceptional character (Red) who claims that being "institutionalized" can keep a man from being truly free.  This movie displays one of the best one-liners I have ever heard and the best ending life has to offer-(if you listen close to what Red has to say he fore shadows Andy's greatest stunt.) I enjoyed SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION and I enjoy IMDB, they display all the memorable quotes that I enjoyed and I gave this movie a Rating of 10!!

title: YES; YES, YES
review:
One of the greatest movie I've seen. It tuched me deep in my heart. Absolutely brilliant.

Congratulations King.

title: A good and entertaining movie
review: The Shawshank Redemption made me spend a good evening when I watched it. Though quiet common, the plot has a good rythm. The beginning of the movie is even very common, with the scene of a murder and the following trial. The story in the prison goes rather slowly. The actors are good, especially Morgan Freeman. It is a good entertainment, but nothing more.

title: Brilliant! The greatest drama since Citizen Kane!
review: Shawshank Redemption is one of the greatest flicks I have ever seen. Morgan freeman and Tim Robbins put on an award-winning performance.  I think this film would have received more Academy Awards if the subject matter had not been so dark and it had not been facing Forrest Gump and Pulp Fiction. I watch this film time and time again and still have the same anxiety of the first time.  I have ruined three video tapes of the Shawshank Redemption by excessive viewing.  Each purchase of a new tape is worth it!

title: The most brilliant movie
review:
This is what it's all about! The creation of a movie that will move us all. A great story, great actors, great filming, but most of all:

A superb plot. Absolutly superb.

title: In my top 10
review: Just saw this for the first time on TV and I will definitely get a DVD copy for watching again and again.  A really great movie! I was mesmerized by Freeman and Robbins acting ability.  I felt like they were my personal friends by the end of the movie.  I could relate to their inner thoughts and deeds.

title: One of the best
review:
I saw this movie for the first time a year and a half ago. I liked it, but I didn't remember how much until it was on TV today. Everything comes together so well at the end, and on repeated viewing, there is a whole new level to it.

Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are both exceptional in their roles. Robbins plays Andy Dufresne, a convicted murderer who goes to Shawshank Prison where he is befriended by Red (Morgan Freeman), who has already served 20 years there. Despite the hardships of prison, Andy refuses to lose hope, and he tries to inspire Red to feel as he does.

I can't think of one scene that was wasted. Everything helped build to the movie's conclusion. Every character was important, as was every line of dialogue.

I actually cried at the end. This movie really makes you think and touches your heart. Next to Pulp Fiction, the best movie of the 90's.

title: An absolutely brilliant adaptation.
review: The Shawshank redemption is one of a very few movies that lives up to the book it is based upon. Many Stephen King books become almost unrecognizable on the screen, but this one, like 'The Green Mile', stays true to the feel and rhythm of the book. Every time I watch it, I appreciate it more. One of the best.

title: GREAT!!!!!!
review: I want to say that this film is one of the best ever:THE REASON IS SIMPLE...........................ACTING IS AWESOME!!!!!!!!!! Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are simply the BEST!!!!!!AS FOR FORREST GUMP.......................DO YOU REALLY BELIEVE THAT IT WAS BETTER THAN THE "SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION"??????NO WAYYYYYYYYYY! FORREST GUMP IS A SIMPLE FRAUD!!!!!!!!TOM HANKS IS AWFUL,AND SO IS THE ENTIRE FILM...................

title: Inside, we are free!
review:
Together with "Papillon", The Shawshank Redemption is the best prison movie ever. It is of the kind that makes a print in memory. There are many stories within one story without disturbing the unity: a perfect stream. The story unfolds in many ways. The stories of the lost souls of modern system..

Dufrane's innocence and neverfading hope, Red's friendship and wisdom, and other characters: all of them are equally important. Watch it several times, you'll find something interesting each time.

You'll think where is the prison: inside or outside? The modern system is such overwhelming, Dufrane cannot escape it even in jail. He has to pay the price of his innocence in such a world. But he decodes the system and prepares his individual salvation to go to the ocean which has no memory. Red is another story: he seems to sink into a total submission and a silent resignation till he sees the neverfading hope of Dufrane. The part where Dufrane plays an Italian song to all locking the door is perfect. And that big tree where Red goes to pick up the money and note Dufrane left: it is unforgettable.

title: Better than the book.
review: You've heard the rule, the book is always better than the movie.  Here is the only exception I have found.  This movie is better than the book.  A great book - Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption, by Stephen King. The movie is even better.  It could well have been named, the Shawshank Exception.

title: One word... Brilliant.
review:
This must be one of the movies I have enjoyed most at the cinema. I can't find one bad moment in this masterpiece. Both Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman delivered their parts as if they were living them. Morgan Freeman's thought's was interesting listening too. My feeling for this film can't be expressed in words so I let the rest of the audience decide whether they like it or not. But as You already imagine, this is one of my favorites.

10 out of 10

A must see......................

title: It doesn't get much better than this.
review:
This is, without a doubt, one of the most gripping movies that I've ever seen. The script is well written and proves once again that Stephen King is a masterful story teller. I've definitely seen a few King movies that have left a bit to be desired, but this is not it. King is at his best on this one.

Let's not forget the stunning performances of Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman. There couldn't be a better pairing then these to gentlemen. This was a defining role for Robbins as he broke out of his typical `funny movie' role and proved without a doubt that he is an actor in every sense of the word. I gained new respect for this man after seeing this movie and gladly see anything he does.

Morgan Freeman succeeded in further cementing himself in my mind as one of the great actors of today. He makes you believe that the saying is true; `They sentence you to life and that's exactly what they get.'

Don't take my word for it, see it for yourself. Don't just rent it, though, buy it because you'll have to own it once you've seen it and there's no sense in throwing away your money on the rental.

title: The Best
review: I have no clever thoughts or ideas about this movie.  I am not going to discuss the plot, acting, or directing.  It is just the best movie I have ever seen.  Period.  End of story.  See ya.  .

title: breath-taking
review: The Shawshank Redemption was a beautifully directed movie. The actors portrayed their characters to the greatest extent and i thoroughly enjoyed this movie. The best scene in the movie was the huge tree...each of its branches catching the suns rays as Morgan Freeman finds what Tim Robbins left for him...anyone who doesn't remember that better watch the movie again.

title: brilliant
review:
This film is based on Stephen King's story Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption. It was part of a collection of four short novels, among them Apt Pupil (adapted by Bryan Singer) and The Body (made into Stand By Me by Rob Reiner). Shawshank was a great story and the film adaption by Frank Darabont is brilliant. The film is highlighted by the strong performances of Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins.

This movie has everything you could want in a film: inspiring story of people persevering through bad times, strong directing and acting (two of the very best actors of today) and one of the classic endings I've seen in a movie.

Shawshank is well-made and inspiring. It has joined my personal movie hall-of-fame, which includes The Grapes of Wrath, High Noon, Goodfellas, L.A. Confidential and Bugsy. I also reccomend The Green Mile, Darabont's most recent King adaption.

title: This movie was brilliant!
review: I really enjoyed this movie. There was obviously a lot of thought put into the script and it delivers brilliantly. The directing is also wonderful, and the actors fit the part perfectly. This is a gruesome account of prison life in the 1950's-60's that is very violent, although this was necessary in the film. A very good movie, and a must-see!

title: The best
review: In my book this is the best movie ever made, or at least my favorite.  I know that may be going out on a limb, but it is that spectacular.  It makes me smile every time in the end, it actually brings me near tears which very few movies have ever done.

title: By far the easiest movie to watch over and over again!
review:
Arguably Tim Robbins' greatest performance to date. Coming from someone who tends to appreciate movies set behind bars, this movie is every bit worth 10 stars! I was astonished to find out that this is adapted from a great Stephen King short story, Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption.

Before writing this review, I sat down, with a bowl of popcorn and a cold one (Pepsi), and watched this great movie again. It has come to my opinion that there is absolutely nothing wrong with this movie, or the way it was put together. Everyone prisoner should be allowed to watch this movie, and hope that their warden would allow them to keep after the books, and then use that position to break out. But, after all, this is Hollywood!

title: Greatest movie ever
review: This is one of the best films I have ever seen in my life the acting and story are superb. If you have not seen this movie go see it RIGHT NOW! This movie has wone 7 Oscars I think and it deserves ever one of them.  Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are a great team together

title: Superb
review: This simply is the best movie I've ever seen. With 2 of the greatest actors (Tim Robbins & Morgan Freeman) and such a great ending, it will be difficult to beat (in my case). This movie will be the standard for 'jail-movies' for a very long time!

title: Wonderful
review: This movie was a little overrated, but it was still wonderful.  What can I say that hasn't already been said.  It was a lot like the Green Mile, only it has some more interesting plot twists and such.  It had a great ending. It deserved to be nominated for Best Picture, and I enjoyed it more than Forrest Gump (which, I think won that year), but I think Pulp Fiction should have won that year.

title: powerful, but could have been less intense
review: There is no doubt in my mind that this is a very powerful and important motion picture.  But, due to the R rating, there are certain situations that are somewhat shocking in nature.  A few cuts might have helped move the story along, too.  Otherwise, an ok film.

title: Simply perfect.
review:
I was so surprised and glad to see this movie as high as it is on this site's list. It is one of my favorite movies and so many people missed out on it because of GUMP, which I personally feel is an inferior movie.

Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman give incredibly moving and restrained performances that moved me to tears more than once. The direction and timing were flawless, and the story itself inspirational. It is so nice to see a Stephen King movie done right for once.

This is simply a wonderful movie, worth watching over and over again.

title: Hands down the Greatest Movie ever made
review:
Perhaps the only thing more remarkable than this masterpiece of a movie is the fact that neither Tim Robbins nor Morgan Freeman won Oscars for their performances. I would put Freeman's portrayal of Ellis Redding amongst the best performances ever in a movie...so moving, so powerful. And the fact that this film did not win Best Picture is all the more unsettling.

This movie isn't just about a couple of guys in prison. Anyone who sees that, well, that must be where the "1" ratings came from. The message of hope is so positively inspiring. This is a movie that immensely impacted my life, something I can't say about any other film. Forrest Gump? Sure it was a good movie, but it really was just about a slow-witted man on a bench discussing his life. It never should have won Best Picture. I'm not sure if the MPAA ever saw this movie, maybe that explains it. Not only was the acting magnificent, but the ending is one of the best in movie history. I'm a 19 year old male, and I can't remember the last time I cried for anything. But the final scene in The Shawshank Redemption reduced me to tears. If there is anyone reading this who has not seen this movie, you would be doing yourself a huge injustice if you didn't run to the video store immediately. I've seen all the "Great" movies -- Citizen Kane, Casablanca, Godfather (not to mention American Beauty, the most overrated movie ever), but none of them even comes so close as to compare to this movie. Plain and simple, the Shawshank Redemption is the best movie I have ever seen, and it will be a very long time before something better comes along. 20/10 if I could.

title: Number 1 ?
review: Someone please tell me why this film is number two when it has a 9.0 user rating. Perhaps the mafia has an insider here to keep the Godfather number 1. Anyway this film deserves to be number 1 for so many reasons. Just see it and you will know why.

title: Beauty
review:
A beautiful film. I must have seen it twenty times. No joke. Thomas Newman's haunting musical score still touches me with every viewing. This is one of those films that plays on TV almost constantly and yet you still find yourself watching it every time. I guess its because of its epic scale and like a great painting you can find some new in it each time you view it.

Frank Darabont does a great adaptation of Stephen King's novella from his 'Different Seasons' collection. I guess the theme of each novella in the book relates to the different seasons. The quote 'hope springs eternal' is at the preface of the Shawshank section of the book and if you've seen the film you know hope is the movie's central theme.

Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins make a great pair in this, probably the best on screen pair since Redford and Newman. See this film and you may become a Shawshank fanatic like so many other people.

title: Gets better every time I watch it
review:
There are so many facets to this film, both subtle and obvious. You really need to see it multiple times to appreciate them all. Several reviews have tried to boil this movie down into a few phrases, usually not doing it justice. This movie is about the growing and intimate friendship of the two main characters, and is possibly the best male friendship movie ever made.

If only Steven King would stick to movies like this and Stand By Me, instead of the supernatural horror films. His story-telling prowess is unmatched.

Morgan Freeman once again shows his incredible abilities, and this performance ranks with his great portrayal in Glory! He has an uncanny knack for helping you know a character better than it's screentime should allow. You just know who Red is in this film, in your heart.

HBO's showing several years ago included a couple of cut-out scenes that were fantastic, and are worth looking for if you like this movie.

title: I really, really like it
review:
I suppose I can't call it the single best film ever, but I really like it. I must admit I don't understand the people who call it too sappy. I'm usually pretty observant about sap, but I find this film truly touching. Well-written, well-filmed, well-acted, it is very moving from beginning to end. Some necessary changes were made from the original novella, such as making it one warden instead of several, changing over time.

The warden, in my opinion, is one of the rare well-made bad guys. You don't like him at all, but he still has human motivations, not super-evil, over-the-top unbelievable qualities. Of course, Red and Andy are both well-crafted characters.

It's a fine, understated film. I think it's one of the best films of the past several years. Good music, too.

One more thing: I saw somewhere the complaint that no one seems to age, though the movie spans several years. While the aging process isn't given the full focus of the film, it's clearly there. I don't think that's a valid complaint. My two cents are now used up.

title: Almost perfect...
review: ...movie and like another of my favorites, "Fried Green Tomatoes," one that I could see over and over again and still find something new to appreciate. This is a jewel of a movie and one that I'm sorry didn't receive the recognition it so richly deserved. James Whitmore should at least have been nominated for Best Supporting Actor; that he didn't is a disgrace. Morgan Freeman gives his usual awesome performance. Rent this movie! Then a few months later, rent it again. This movie is so poignant and says so much about friendship and hope that I defy anyone not to be moved by it.

title: A lesson in film making!
review: If more people would watch the Shawshank Redemption before putting on a film maker hat and providing the public with the crud that's out there, I am convinced that the world would be a much better place! This film is just simply UNREAL! Great job all around and no wonder it's in the top 5 of the IMDB's all time best 100.

title: An inspirational reflection of life's own tribulations
review:
This and Clint Eastwood's "Unforgiven" rank side by side at the summit of my all-time favorites list (and no, I am not a Morgan Freeman freak).

This is the kind of movie that starts out solid and keeps driving at you...solid. It does not make any insultingly wrongful turns in logic nor does it infringe on your conception of what is believable and what is excruciatingly unbelievable.

This is a no-frills story of a man who is wrongfully accused of murdering his wife. The film's glorious irony, that his 19-years-long jail sentence is the best thing to happen to him in his life, slowly manifests itself.

title: A spectacular debut unfortunately followed by a lackluster sophomore effort
review: After being slightly dissappointed by "The Green Mile", I decided to check out Frank Darabont's first adaptation of a Steven King prison story once again. "The Shawshank Redemption" remained as much of an enjoyably original modern classic after this second viewing. In this second viewing, I appreciated even more the sparklingly sharp dialogue between Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins. Like in "Green Mile", Darabont set the scene of a depression-era prison extremely well. The director was also well-served to use King's vivid character descriptions to make the supporting characters as memorable as the leads. The result was an instant, uplifting classic about hope brought to the most hopeless locations.

title: Well deserving of it's number 2 IMDb ranking!
review: I do not normally consider myself to be much of a drama fan, having always preferred the action-adventure genre. "The Shawshank Redemption" is the film that changed that feeling for me, and reading the other comments and reviews, for a lot of other people as well.  Frank Darabont made a giant leap forward from his previous efforts in the "B" horror film world when he came up with this gem.  Tim Robbins turned in his best performance as Andy Dufresne, and Morgan Freeman was brilliantly cast as Red.  This is a "Feel-Good" movie of the first order, and well worth it's number 2 ranking on the IMDb top 250.  Everything works in this film, the score, the acting, the realism of the prison scenes, absolutely  everything!  "Shawshank" is as close to a perfect film as you will ever see.  If you do not already own a copy of this masterpiece, run, do not walk, to the video store and purchase a copy.  It should be in the library of every movie fan.  A 5 star, 10 out of 10, classic movie!!

title: man!!
review: this is the greatest movie i have ever seen.  by reading the plot you may think of it as just another prison movie. it's more of a friends movie. the greatest portrayal of how wonderful a friend is i have ever seen.  i love this movie and have seen it a million times and will see it another million times.

title: Best Prison Movie Ever? Heck, Best Movie Ever. Period.
review:
Okay, I will not reiterate what praises others have said about this movie. I think it's brilliant and touching, and others have expressed this more eloquently than I can. See for yourself.

I just wish IMDB had a 1 to 100 scale for rating movies, instead of 1 to 10. Then I could give this movie a perfect 100, while giving something like "Cinema Paradiso" a 94 or 95. As it stands, I gave both movies a ten, but I think Shawshank is a shade better, and I wish a new ratings could reflect that opinion.

title: Inspiring, fulfilling; the best movie I've ever seen
review:
For me, the best movies inspire emotion. This movies does just that for me, better than any other movie to date.

The message here is one of mostly one of hope with a dash of justice thrown in. There is hope for the unjustly incarcerated, and justice for those who do wrong. Andy DeFresne, despite all the odds against him, never lets the situation get to him. Red finds his hope through Andy.

The onscreen performances are superb. Every character has dimension and adds to the message. The screenplay, the most important component of any movie, is simply flawless.

title: The Greatest Film Ever? Could Be.
review:
For those who have not seen The Shawshank Redemption, you have, so far, missed a genuine treat. I have seen hundreds of films. I don't think I have ever seen more than two or three that combined what I consider to be the five basic aspects requisite for consideration as a masterpiece. This is one of those films. The five basic elements are great acting--in which we the viewer see the character, feel the character, not the actor; a great score/sound-track; a cinematic quality that enables the viewer to experience the surroundings, not just view them; great dialogue and non-dialogue--the best scripts usually utilize not only the verbal abilities of actors, but non-verbal expression as well (see a film with Cary Grant or Robert De Niro to know what I mean); and most important a compelling story.

The Shawshank Redemption not only offers ALL of these, but does so at a level few films have ever reached.

The basic plot is simple enough: a man is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and the man with whom she is having an affair. Why then is it so great? The performances, all around, but especially of Robbins and Freeman are so rich, so human, the viewer feels they are living their experiences. The film demonstrates, magnificently, how a man can create a meaningful life against horrid (mentally and physically) circumstances. The film wrenches the guts of its viewers, yet provides great satisfaction in the end. It is a great film celebrating determination, friendship, revenge (as sweet as you will ever see), education, and the basic goodness intrinsic to all people.

title: 9, not 10
review:
This is the film I always heard people talk about but never saw.

Until now. I must say, it does fulfil my expectations. It has been

brilliantly directed, the actors have done a wonderful job and

the story is perfect. I recommend it to everybody.

But... yes there is a but, I thought it just missed a little

something. That's the reason I gave it a 9 instead of a 10. This

film is a product of craftmanship, but it isn't art. And this is

what makes a film truly great. Everything has been put in the

right place, but it misses some originality, some magic touch.

It's a brilliant movie, but it doesn't compare to other movies

like American Beauty or American History X, which truly change

your way of thinking.

title: Simply The Best?
review: I have many films that I regard as my personal favourites and it is difficult to put these in any order.  However the number one in my list is easy - The Shawshank Redemption. This film has addictive qualities - if this film is on a screen you have to watch it no matter how often you've seen it. I think I'll go and watch it again now!

title: If ever a film deserved a bag of Oscars, this is it!
review:
When one thinks of how many dross films have somehow managed to win Oscars you begin to lose faith when the classic SR doesn't even win one.

For the life of me I don't know why this film was overlooked - sure the critics didn't like it, and it didn't do too well at the Box Office because the title was just too difficult or ambiguous to remember. Nevertheless by the time it went to Video the film has had a second life to the point where it is in the top three films of all time according to the members of IMDb, and rightly so.

Prison films are nothing new of course, and neither is SR. But SR shines from so many areas that it has to be the best prison film ever.

I was particularly impressed with the cinematography from Roger Deakins, especially those wonderful sweeping pan shots from of the prison taken from above.

The acting is a revelation from all concerned especially Morgan Freeman who really should have won an Oscar. But then there's Robbins himself who I've never really warmed to, except perhaps for Jacobs Ladder. But he really is a tour-de-force here and should be proud of this film.

But the acting plaudits go deeper than just the two main stars; the support from Bob Gunton, William Sadler & especially Clancy Brown also deserve huge credit.

Its a very hard, uncompromising film but it doesn't play to stereotype. The violence is very real and yet warranted I think.

It does fall to the cliche trap on one or two occasions - the ending, although generally well done, was perhaps just a little pretencious for my liking, especially the preachy monologue from Freeman jarred just a tad.

Another annoying thing is the ageing process. Robbins hardly ages at all during his 20 year stay...but I'm quibbling.

SR is a superb, moving & rewarding film full of hope & belief. The sudden surge of emotional energy that went through me as Robbins stands in the pool, his arms outstretched as the rain lashes down on him!

In my virtual world The Shawshank Redemption won 10 Oscars and became a Box Office champ and was loved by the critics. The real world, just like the real world outside Shawshank Prison, is simply too cruel to want to think about!

title: well done prison film
review: An intelligent, resourceful man survives in a brutal prison during the 1950's and 60's. Emphasis on character development rather than enviroment place this film ahead of others in this genre.  A fine example of the triumph-of-human-spirit-over-adversity theme. (Rating: A)

title: Great and beautiful
review:
This film is so beautiful and so touching I had problems seeing it without crying. Who knew Stephen King could write like this and the first film of Frank Darabont(later he directed The Green Mile)was to be one of the greatest films ever made. Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins are excellent in this movie and the way the story itself is told is pure genius.

It`s a brutal and violent film ,but still it`s the most beautiful and loving film I`ve ever seen. It`s a story about friendship and hope and the road to freedom.The greatest scene in the film is when Andy and his fellow-prisoners work at the roof,and Andy is nearly killed by captain Hadley, but ends up drinking beer in the morning sun with his friends "like free men".

title: A human being's spirit can be the most powerful thing of all.
review: An all-time favorite.  I am a college professor, and have used this film in sociology, science of success, and various legal classes that I teach.  The reactions of students are almost always extremely poignant.  An inspirational prison movie.  Unbelieveable.

title: A fantastic, powerful film.
review: This film is destined to become a classic. It shows the human spirit in full force. The story is terrific with many wonderful characters. Morgan Freeman delivers a truly brilliant performance that received a well-deserved Academy Award nomination. Bob Gunton gives a wonderfully villainous, intense performance as Warden Norton. Darabont's direction is solid. The climax is wonderfully uplifting. On a personal note, I thought this film slowed down at times but these sequences were essential to the plot, they just seemed to distract me. This film is definetly worth a look.

title: Emotional Powerhouse
review:
I remember wanting to see this movie because I saw the promotional shot of Robbins standing in the rain; I thought it was a beautiful scene. It is a minor scene in the movie.

This movie is, for lack of a better word, perfect. Every moment holds meaning, every performance is dead on. I have watched it more times than I can count, and it always seems new and wonderful to me. More than any movie I have seen, it brings real emotions to the audience and brings comfort to the hopeless.

Sometimes I think a great work of art is one that brings change to the audience. This movie is transforming.

title: This Movie Rules the World
review: This is the best movie ever made.  If you haven't seen it yet, stop doing whatever it is that you are doing, go to your local video store, shell out the three or four dollars to rent the videotape or DVD, go home, put some popcorn in the microwave, put the movie in, turn on your home entertainment center, sit on the couch, and WATCH THIS MOVIE.  If you have friends who haven't seen it yet, tell them to come over and watch it with you.  You will not be disappointed.  They will not be disappointed.  This is the best movie ever made.

title: Calling it a masterpiece is an understatement
review: This movie is brilliant.  There is no need to go into detail about the reasons behind my saying so.  It is a film that everyone should simply take the time out to watch- to try to describe its qualities would be at best an injustice to this piece of treasure.  I have never encountered a single person who regretted watching the film, and come on lets give it some more 10s so it can beat out the godfather! (which I haven't seen so maybe once I do I'll be singing a different tune)...but regardless, this film is amazing, and not many can compare to it at all.

title: 5 out of 5 stars !!!!
review:
This film ranks as one of my top 10 films of all time .

Superb performances by Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins , they cast this film wonderfully , From the crafty warden , to the prison guards , to all the inmates , And what a terrific ending to a superb film .

This film was nominated for Best Picture but lost to Forrest Gump , had it not been for Gump , this film would have surely won Best Picture.

I have watched this film 20 or so times and never get tired of it , No question it is the best Prison Film ever made ( Escape from Alcatraz close second ).

title: What can I say...
review: This film is, with no shadow of a doubt what so ever, the best movie that I have ever had the wonderous pleasure to view. Films like Shawshank are what allow me to love movies and to cherish wonderful stories. I can say that I'm a critical gremlin- I'm constantly attempting to find faults, flaws and plot holes in every movie i see- yes, I'm that guy who always says it was only an ok movie when you loved it- But... this one is so powerful, so beautiful, so absolutely inspiring that I couldn't care if there was a plot hole or a flaw, its just too good of a film to attack. To Hell with Forest Gump for winning over Shawshank, to Hell with Titanic, Shakespeare in garbage, The English Idiot, and Forest Dump- these movies all sucked, sucked, sucked to begin with but compared to the diamond jewel of Shawshank, they look as good as sitcoms made by Fox. So anyway, my favorite movie of all time and only one of three movies worthy of a ten rating.

title: read the other reviews!
review: i really dont have any more to say - except read the other reviews - they really say it for me. In other words - this is one of the greatest movies of all time. This is an absolute masterpiece and it will be definitely a film that i will gladly show to my grandchildren in the mid-21st century - IT'S THAT GOOD... watch it and learn.....

title: Magnificent movie...the best I've seen!
review: It's a great thing when you can finally find a movie you can definitively call "your favorite".  This is mine.  "The Shawshank Redemption", based on Stephen King's short novella entitled "Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption", is an excellent adaptation of said literature...I will go out and say it; I've read the story and seen the movie, and although the movie took some parts out (in the story, there were three different wardens over the course of the story, and Red was Irish, not black), it expanded the detail greatly, covering parts the novella never bothered to touch on (such as Andy getting a new set of clothes and a shiny pair of shoes from the Warden ^_^).  The characters are all detailed and alive, not once did I find a character unbelievable. And I've never EVER seen an ending so incredible.  My eyes were wide, I was chanting "Oh My God" over and over...This movie makes you feel good all over and gives you a new perspective on life and freedom. This movie is nothing short of a masterpiece.  The only fault I find is that it came out at the time as Forrest Gump, which had a lot more advertising and thus beat this great movie out in the box office.  Had it come out a few months later, it would have been much more successful.

title: Truly unforgettable!!
review:
Based on Stephen Kings novel, this film tells the tale of a man (Tim Robbins in excellent form), sentanced to 2 life sentances for the double murder of his wife and her lover.

Inside he meets Red (Morgan Freeman) and over the next 20 years tells the story of his life and the lives around him.

This is not a very happy movie although (turn away if you dont want any idea of the ending) has a happy ending. Thats a double negative, but the film shows the graphic violence of prisons in the 1940's, where men are forcefully raped.

Two lines (both spoken by Freeman) really stand out in this film. See if you know what they are.

10/10

title: Brilliant Redemptive Epic
review:
This film is truly one of the greatest of all time. Much like the other works based on Stephen King novels, there is a main storyline to follow, and then another deeper story.

Morgan Freeman does a very impressive job portraying a man who has been held prisoner by his own fear of the outside world, and who is eventually freed by hope. Tim Robbins also did an excellent job, but Frank Darabont really deserves a lot of credit for fleshing out this beautifully written script into a great movie.

This is a movie that warrants multiple viewings. Four stars!

title: The Most Worthy of All Movies!
review: This was one of the very first movies that got me choked up.  I first saw it on a Pay television network, then decided that I had to have it.  To think that such a worthy film in all categories (Acting, Directing, Etc.) did not receive not one Oscar.  Yes! I was p***ed off as well.  It was much better that Forrest Gump, but hey I don't decide what wins and what doesn't. This is a definite movie for everyone!

title: Outstanding, simply outstanding!
review: All my friends had the same reaction to this movie as I did when first viewing it .. how come I never heard more about it? It was great! The acting was fantastic. The storyline flowed perfectly. The writing and editing couldn't have been better.  Clearly, if not pitted against "Forrest Gump", "Little Women", "Nell", "Quiz Show" and "Pulp Fiction" (wow, what a line-up), I'm sure this movie would have won more awards. Morgan Freeman was great, and Tim Robbins was nothing short of amazing. If you like acting, this movie is a must!

title: A real good movie.
review: I have read the short story (novella?) by Steven King and seen this great film and I have to say that this is one time when Hollywood did a better job then the author. I've seen tons of prison movies (some with good plots and others that are complete B movies) and this has to be the best one out there. Usually when I like a movie, I can watch it a bunch of times. And I have seen Shawshank many times, but none of the repeated viewings were as good as the first. Clancy Brown (he was great in Highlander too) once again steals the show as a Hard A--- prison guard who gets his just desserts in the end. Chances are you've already seen this, but if you haven't, I fully recommend you give it a chance.

title: My Favorite Film
review: The Shawshank Redemption was a film that I was always on my way to the theater to see, but unfortunately, I got sidetracked each and every time. Critics felt that the long title kept people away, I guess I was in that category, no matter how great I heard this movie was. I finally saw the movie the day it hit videotape. To this day, it continues to dominate the number one position on my list of favorite films of all time. There is so much to love about this film. Especially the writing by Frank Darabont. This is one of the few films that does Stephen King's material justice. It's a very uplifting story, one that you can't really articulate with words. This film is about the experience. I'm proud to say that I own a copy of the movie, a copy of the screenplay, and a copy of Different Seasons, in which the original story derived. This is the one picture I recommend to people, even strangers, on a regular basis.

title: A true modern day classic!
review: To begin with,  The story is pretty well cliched.  Like most prison dramas hope and struggle seem to be the element that put the plot together.  For once this is probably the one time that such a cliched plot actually worked. I have personally seen this movie over 20 times just to figure out how and why it works so well.  First of all the story is deep and thought provoking. Morgan Freeman's voice over narrative lets you see it through his eyes (the movie is really about him).  The acting is flawless the whole picture is shot as a true epic.  This is one great film about friendship and hope that does not dwell to much on pathos and mindless sentimentality.  A true modern day classic!

title: A moment of Cinematic genius!
review: I remember seeing The Shawshank Redemption back in '94 and thinking how absolutely out of the ordinary it was for a Hollywood picture. No soft soap ending, no moral message and no "Whey-hey isn't America great" that you usually get from Hollywood pics. The fact its a Steven King is remarkable to, out of his usual style, I think. It's photographed beautifully and makes no bones about the harsh reality of prison. I don't really know much about Frank Dufont but I would really like to see his other pictures based on the strength of this one.

title: The best film of all time.
review: It is almost impossible to glorify this movie more than it deserves because, simply I believe it is the greatest ever made. The story, characters, music are absolutely mesmerizing. The story of the never say die hope of a wrongfully convicted man sent to prison for life is awe-inspiring and poignant.  Watch this with someone you love and cherish. **** stars

title: Simple, powerful and a masterpiece
review:
This movie is absolutely superb. You watch it and all the simple, unremarkable details just cumulate and you realise that this movie, by being unflashy and ordinary is telling a powerful story about hope and redemption. Andy seems to be the main character but it is Red who finds himself, who is redeemed.

The Shawshank Redemption was overlooked because it looked unremarkable. But this movie has to be seen. My friends are action movie fanatics but they were all stunned by this movie. Stephen King should be thanked for writing the novella and the director should be praised for bringing it to the screen in such fine form. Forget Forrest Gump, this was the Best Picture of 1994.

title: One Of The Best Movies I Have Ever Seen.
review:
Morgan Freeman at his absolute best, Tim Robbins - better than ever - it must be a good film!!

The Shawshank Redemption grabs you tight and pulls you into its depth and drama. It is definitely worth a look if you haven't seen it.

This film shows the story of how hope can set you free. It is a beautiful film with excellent actors, an good story and shocking (but excellent) dialouge.

The Shawshank Redemption definitely deserves it's place as my no. 5 favourite film and IMDb's no. 3 user rated film.

My rating : Obviously 10/10.

title: Fantastic Film
review:
I happened to see this film on TV not too long ago. My husband was watching so I thought I would sit down and watch. I was absolutely blown away by this film Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman were super!! It was well acted well edited. This is one of the most outstanding movies I have seen in recent years.

I purchased the video and have watched numerous times. The conclusion of this film had me on the edge of my seat. JUST OUTSTANDING!

title: The Perfect Movie
review:
This would have to be THE best movie that I have ever seen. The story of a wrongly convicted man. And the story of a man searching for meaning. And the story of an institutionalised man. This movie takes several different stories and turns them into one fantastic film.

Watch it a number of times to see all the stories come together in an inspiring manner that touches the soul. I can't recommend this movie enough. Morgan Freeman's performance of the narrating Red, and explanations of prison life are truly touching. Tim Robbins' portrayal of Andy is near perfect, no, it IS perfect.

Watch it, then watch it again.

You won't be disappointed.

title: A testament to the spirit of Hope...
review:
Locked in the confines of prison, one expects the insanities to unfold, to break the human spirit and rape it of its essence, but one thing above all else allows survival for even the misjudged guilt of one man who must wake up to realize the awful truth. That thing is hope, and it breathes through every inch of this movie, as well as a sensational feeling of greatness.

Every moment and every bit of emotion is genuine, well spent. The whole feel and experience of it all will not only touch the little person inside us all, but will also give you a taste of a great story and masterful film making. I have always loved this movie, from the moment I first saw it in theaters, and every further time I see it when watching it from my video collection.

Films like this continue to inspire me in my own endeavours, to fully engross me within its stone walls, to make me realize every bit how precious freedom truly is. May this movie live on in the collections of everyone, and may no person have to experience even a fraction of the pain and suffering found in this great film...

title: A marvel of filmmaking...
review:
As near to perfect as a movie can get, "The Shawshank Redemption" is absolutely superlative entertainment. I keep wondering at those who claim the movie is too long (as many also did for the fantastic "Green Mile"). I wonder if MTV, television newscasts, commercials and other things have destroyed the attention span of several generations of people. Nobody seems to be able to stick with anything for more than an absolute maximum of two hours anymore. It's a disappointing trend, because often a great story cannot be told in the usual 120-minute maximum alloted to most films.

If you have the attention span to watch a film longer than two hours, movies just don't get any better than this one does. Don't look for realism (try PBS or any documentary for that), look for plot, acting talent and (above all): Simply a good, satisfying tale! The Shawshank Redemption has it all, in spades, and Frank Darabont is on his way to an absolutely stellar directing career. Kudos to Stephen King as well for his excellent novella, "Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption," which obviously helped make this film possible. 10/10.

title: Great movie with great performances!!!
review: This is a story with drama, injustice, pain and real friendship. Both performances ( Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins ) were wonderful, they have made the movie even more interesting!!! No doubt, one of my favourites so far...really it is just to watching it too many times with no possibility of getting bored!!!

review:

title: Just who is the hero?
review:
As stated in the tagline, this is a film of hope. The difficult question is however, is whom does it refer to? The two lead characters (Andy Dufresne and 'Red' Redding, played superbly by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman respectively) are both inmates at Shawshank penitentiary, one innocent and the other guilty. This however, does not mar your opinion of either character - you are able to sympathise with both of them, as you are with many of the prisoners. You root for these criminals every inch of the way, despite their wayward past and current situations. This is perhaps the ultimate feelgood movie, with the greatest twist since Kevin Spacey walked away in The Usual Suspects. Unlike other films of this genre however, there is no need for constant assurance that this will make you feel good - bar one or two moments in the middle, there is no hint that anything positive will happen to either hero, right up until that moment.

The greatest factor in this movie must be the characterisation. Prison guards turn from monsters, to friends to cowards; prisoners range from the horrific, to cruel, to pitiful and finally to likable. Above all, unlike too many recent films, each and every character is human and believable.

Is there an answer to that question? Which character has the lead - the narrating Red or the centrepiece Andy? Who has the hope? The answer to that lies in the interpretation of a film that can mean anything.

title: Beautiful in its restraint.
review:
Being the cynic that I am, it's my inclination to look for the weaknesses of films that ultimately detract from their overall quality. How refreshing it is that, on occasion, a film is so masterfully crafted that I can simply take in all that it has to offer. Such is the case with _The Shawshank Redemption_.

And with _The Shawshank Redemption_, it isn't an issue of the excellence of the different components of the film; instead, it's an issue of the way that all of the elements of this movie-- the writing, directing, and acting-- are so vastly superior to those of most every other film.

It's difficult to imagine two things more cliched than "Prison Dramas" and films about "The Triumph of the Human Spirit." Though _The Shawshank Redemption_ certainly qualifies as both of those cinematic cliches, there's nothing about the film that seems even the least bit tired. The unique characters of Red and Andy Dufrense bring an unexpected liveliness to a film that could have easily been both obvious and trite-- such as _The Green Mile_.

Because of the intelligently-written screenplay, with its engaging plot twists and historically appropriate dialogue, coupled with truly remarkable performances by both Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman that convey all of the depth and honesty of their challenging characters, _Shawshank_ improves upon the repeated viewings that are necessary to take in all that it has to offer. The unparalleled depth of this movie allow the viewer to gain something new-- and something ultimately positive-- from each additional viewing.

Perhaps the greatest achievement of _The Shawshank Redemption_ is the restraint that director Frank Darabont uses in unfolding this multifaceted story. When approaching a film with even a fraction of the thematic load of this one, most directors simply succumb to the too-easy temptation to tack a didactic, heavy-handed morality statement onto the last sequence. Darabont attains a rare closure; he _doesn't_ moralize. He allows the viewer to make his/her own judgments about each of the characters and the fate that he ultimately meets over the course of the film.

RATING: 10 out of 10. In a decade, _The Shawshank Redemption_ will be grouped into the cinematic canon alongside such triumphs as _Citizen Kane_ and _Dr. Strangelove_. It's not an unmerited distinction. An example of truly flawless filmmaking.

title: Excellent! Definitely on my top ten list!
review: Only those who have been in prison can appreciate best the dreams and hopes that keep folks in there going. Most are merely pipe dreams - never to be realised. I think this flick hits the nail on the head, pardon the cliché. 10 outta 10!

title: You shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free
review: I have no doubt in saying that this is undoubtedly the best movie I have ever seen. "The Shawshank Redemption" is a tale of suffering and despair, but also one of hope and redemption - as the title suggests. The truth of life lies within each one of us - just as it lay within Andy Dufresne - all we have to do is find it. Once you know the truth, it will set you free. The message of this film is that there is always hope, there is always truth, and together these two bring redemption - even in Shawshank!

title: Ranks right up there with To Kill a Mockingbird
review: At the risk of gushing... I just have to comment that this film takes my breath away every time I watch it.  I can never seem to pass by the channel when it's on TV.  I cry every time I see it.  It's a good cry though, a "feeling something" cry.  Sometimes in the rush of daily life you can forget what it's like to simply FEEL your emotions.  As other people have said here - each time you watch this film, more layers of story are revealed to you. The whole experience of it -- the music, the atmospheric, this-feels-like-a-real-place setting, the poetic quality of Morgan Freeman's narration (and what a voice he has!), the characters who seem like real people instead of stereotypes, and the theme of the survival of hope even in the most oppressive of circumstances -- is very spiritual. I experience the gamut of emotions during this film but wind up feeling inspired and uplifted.  I feel as though I've taken the journey beside Andy and Red. This movie does indeed stay with you; you find yourself pondering its elements and marvelling at its beautiful simplicity.  It's a movie that requires you to pay close attention and I certainly agree that more than one viewing is necessary to appreciate everything it wants to offer to the viewer.  What a treasure this movie is.  May it be preserved well!!!!  I hope... I hope...

title: Classic!
review: I'm kind of lost for words for this movie. I saw it last night on my DVD-player and what I saw was brilliance. The story is about a banker Andy (Tim Robbins) who get prisoned for murdering his wife and her secret lover. In prison he says he's innocent, which makes the other inmates break out in laughter. No one is innocent in prison they say. `They've all been f***ed by lawyers.' What follows is a fight for justice. A inmate (George Freeman) who calls himself Red (the other inmates call him that because he's `irish') finds something special in Andy. They connect soon and becomes good friends. What strikes me about the main characters is that hope and belief is something that they always have. Even though they go through some very tough times in prison, they always have that good confidence in themselves. Go see this movie, if you love the concept of feeling free. There's no let downs or grief ending this movie. You have to see it for yourself.

title: A heartwarming tale of hope and human spirit
review: Hope, love, belief, friendship, feeling. Watch this film and re-establish once again what is good about the movies. If you don't particularly like watching films, I urge you to watch this and experience something unlike you have experienced before. This, alongside AMERICAN BEAUTY, is one of the greatest films ever made.

title: Flawless
review: Any movie that you can see over 30 times and doesn't get old, doesn't become prone to having mistakes found in it and still keeps you anticipating the ending even though you know what's going to happen is a great movie. Flawless is the only word I can use to describe this movie.  From the acting of Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins to the screen play by Stephen King, this film doesn't have one flaw in it.  This film has one of the all time best endings if not the best ending I've ever seen.  A definite master piece of a movie.

title: A classic that is under-appreciated.
review: This movie is definitely on my best of the decade list.  It borrows heavily from a couple movies and makes a fresh, dramatic approach to story telling. Excellent directing, writing, and acting.  Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are awesome in this film.  This is film-making at its best.  I own the VHS and DVD versions of this film, and I highly recommend this film to everyone.

title: In my top 3 of the best movies of all time.
review: This is one of the best movies of all time; an absolute masterpiece!  It brings me to tears every time I see it and I never tire of it.  It is a shame that this movie came out in 1994 because Pulp Fiction and Forrest Gump stole it's thunder.  Had it been released in '95, '96, '98, or '99.  It surely would have been a front runner the best picture oscar.  I exclude '97 because nothing could have beat the almighty Titanic.  Everyone should see this movie because it is the best example of good people triumphing over evil and that hope still exists.  The ending will put you in a good mood, I guarantee it!

title: just to say...
review: I love just drifting through the IMDb just to read others opinions on certain movies, and having checked out the comments on Shawshank Redemption, I'm amazed that some of the latest reviews are from people who have who have only just watched it in the last few weeks. I'm even more pleased that they acknowledge it as one of the best films made, and that it lived up to the hype that has passed via word of mouth. It is a criminal offence that it did not win a single Oscar but at least it not one of those films that will be classed as an undiscovered gem. Career best performances are brought out of all members of the cast: Clancy Brown, Bill Gunton and Bill Sadler will surely never hit those heights again. It may not have been a box office hit but all associated with the movie should feel proud. The cliche is true of The Shawshank Redemption: they don't make them like that any more. Spread the word!

title: AWESOME!
review: Ya know, I never heard of the Shawshank Redemption before I came to the IMDB. I looked at the top 250 and saw it ahead of 1994's Forrest Gump and in the number 2 spot all time and thought, "man, what is this?" I found out a couple weekends ago and I'm not in the least bit disapointed. It was great, I loved it. I can say nothing that hasn't been said already. Great film, I wish I had seen it earlier. Awesome! Haven't seen it? SEE IT!

title: nothing out of place. it all fits together perfectly
review: this movie is one of only 3 that I have on dvd right now, and I am so glad that I own it.  anyone who is a movie fan of any kind should see this. this is an amazing movie shows what someone can do when they hope.  andy duphresne was a character who had hope and kept it alive for 20 years even though he was in prison for life with a crime he didn't commit.  every aspect of this movie: the camera work, the acting, the dialogue, and the story work together in a perfect blend of drama.  the best part was when red came in for his 3rd parole hearing.  his first 2 times, he had just told them what he thought they wanted to hear.  "yes, I believe that i'm entirely cured.  i believe that i am no longer a danger to society."  he was rejected those 2 times.  but the third he was honest, and the outcome was far different.  A nearly perfect movie.

title: Poetry in Motion Pictures
review: Getting to see The Shawshank Redemption was for me a lengthy process, but when I finally caught it it was more than worth the wait. In the history of movies there have been many impressive debuts from promising directors. With The Shawshank Redemption, Frank Darabont has vaulted himself into the ranks of Orson Welles and John Huston. There has not been a more memorable movie experience in the last decade, and it gratifies me to see that users of this site regard this film as highly as it ought to be.

title: Perfect Film
review:
What can you say about a movie that is perfect? I myself have plenty to say. I believe The Shawshank Redemption is the best film ever made because it towers above other films in all respects, directorial ability, acting ability, the story, everything. Director Frank Darabont captured the essence of the hopelessness (or supposed hopelessness) of a dark and desolate prison.

Morgan Freeman shines in a supporting role, and Tim Robbins sets the standards for everything a lead actor should be. His performance was so good, so heartfelt, that every time I see the film I feel like I'm the one fighting his battle. The entire theme of the film, hope, is so overwhelmingly powerful. Based on Stephen King's short story, Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption, the idea of finding hope in a world where life itself is gone is beyond the realms of emotion, it can't be said with words the impact this film makes. Everyone gets what they deserve in the end, and the glorification of triumph and the conquering of fears go beyond imaginable. As a young lady at 16, I have much trouble sometimes finding something to hold onto since falling into a monotonous routine. This film reminds me of the good things in life and that every day is a new one, and is something to be cherished. Thank God that in a world of shoot-em-up, sex and drug filled, ridiculous films some people still see the true meaning of movie making, to change the lives of those watching. If you have never seen The Shawshank Redemption, please do. It is a film of such epic proportions that it moves your soul.

title: Should you see this movie?
review:
After hearing all of the comments on this one, such as, "Greatest Ever Made," "I loved it," "why didn't it win movie of the year?" I had very high expectations upon seeing it.

I was not in the least disappointed. This movie IS all it's made up to be. Yes, without a doubt, you SHOULD see this movie.

The story is a thought-provoking one of hope, and how to find meaning in order in the apparent chaos of life. Andy escapes from the prison in an attempt to find himself, after his good friend Brooks, who has been released after decades of living in the prison, runs into bad fortune. Andy's other friend who is also released manages to find himself like Andy did through his help. This is a story of the torture humans inflict on one another and how it is escaped through hope.

10/10

title: Positive, and to the point.
review: Wonderful, wonderful movie, one of the greatest stories ever told. Terrific acting, and some of the best dialogue that I have ever heard before in a movie.  Brillant screenplay and excellent directing.  Why didn't this movie win Best Picture?

review: I had heard so many good things about this movie, that I just had to see it. I was not disappointed.  This is probably one of the best movies I have ever seen. Period.  Tim Robbins was outstanding, simply outstanding. Morgan Freeman was wonderful and I did not know that Gil Bellows had so much in him.  This movie was absolutely breathtaking.  The scenery, the realism, the characters, everything was simply outstanding.  I sat through the entire movie, spellbound by the whole thing, and then I rewound it and watched again.  I've seen 6 times since, and I always find new and wonderful things everytime I see it.  I loved it.  It was amazing.  This movie is not just about prison, but it's about friendship.  A 20-year-long friendship between two inmates.  I recommend this movie for anyone who needs to find out what real friendship is all about.  This is truly one of the best movies ever.

title: Hope is a good thing, Brooks was wrong...
review: This is my favorite movie of all time. It is about one man's struggle of trying to cope with his life in prison sentence for a crime he didnt commit. This movie make prisoners look like true human beings, not just savages. You really learn about each of the characters. Morgan Freeman gives a great role as Red, who stands by Andy in every instance.

This film sortta runs along and while your watching you dont know why your watching but you cant stop and then when it finishes you think WOW and have the funny feelin in the pit of your stomach and all up your spine, the feelin you get when you know you have watched a cinema masterpiece, i only wish i had been able to see this in the movies rather than on vhs, but it will soon become an addition to my dvd collection.

title: A superb production makes Shawshank a must-see!
review:
The Shawshank Redemption is a movie about personal disaster, misery, impossible difficulties, and eventual triumph. In other words, it's about life.

Tim Robbins plays Andy Dufresne, a young banker convicted of murdering his wife and her lover, and sent to the Shawshank Prison in Maine for life. There he meets Red, an older con played by Morgan Freeman. From there on, the movie is viewed through the eyes of Red, and Freeman's moving commentary surfaces during key points in the flick. Most of the movie is about the friendship between Andy and Red, and the different travails they encounter. The two learn about the meaning of hope, and how one must keep going despite the odds.

All this sounds pretty pat and boring, but the movie most assuredly is not. It has a brilliant mixture of brutal violence, gentle lyricism and uplifting moments coming from the most unusual of places. This could only work with a top-notch group of actors. The inhuman actions of Captain Hadley (Clancy Brown) are enough to turn your head from the screen. This is tempered by the relaxed friendship between Freeman and Robbins, as well as the camaraderie inside Red's group; William Sadler as the stuttering Heywood is terrific. James Whitmore is touching as Brooks, the oldest inmate who is so used to prison life that he can't leave. Gil Bellows (Tommy) has a small but pivotal role; his superb performance changes the momentum of the entire movie. And the triumvirate of Brown, Mark Rolston (Bogs), and Bob Gunton (Warden Norton) set the tone of evil in the prison that only the wiles of Andy and the compassion of Red can surmount.

Some critics say that the movie is too slow. It's slow like a baseball game; its leisurely pace is belied by the amount of strategy underneath. An important moment happens in almost every scene, whether it's Brooks crying, Red making a joke, or Andy slyly getting the best of the system, the end gradually creeps up on us until the surprising, heartwarming finale. The last scene is one of incredible cinematic restraint; the camera actually pulls away from the action, preventing us from seeing the expressions on the characters' faces. We strain to see, not because we need to know what they are feeling--we already know. We just want to see as much as we can because it is so wonderful.

I haven't said much about what happens in the movie. Let's just say that it shows how one's mind and knowledge are more powerful than concrete walls, mental intimidation or physical force.

The Shawshank Redemption was not seen by as many people as it should have been, undoubtedly because of its un-sexy title. Don't be turned off. It's one of those movies that can draw you in and give you a lift, no matter what kind of mood you're in. It's one of the most satisfying movie experiences I've ever had. See it.

title: Easy to like
review:
It was really very easy to like this film - in fact, it was impossible for me NOT to like it. Maybe the key is the phenomenon that is called "lagom" in Sweden. That word doesn't exist in any other language, but it means something like "just right". Not too much, not to little.

I felt very comfortable after watching this film. It didn't change my life, didn't start a revolution - it was just a very good film!

Actually, the end was a bit unexpected. It gave the film a romantic touch that otherwise wouldn't have been there. The only bad thing is that I found details in the story too improbable, and that was a disturbing moment in that type of film. It wouldn't have mattered in an action-filled story, but now it made me irritated, because it stole attention from the story!! Anyway that detail doesn't stop me from really recommending this film - its simply "just right"!

title: This movie is better than the novel
review: That's my feeling when I finished reading the novel recently. Frank Darabont obviously made a lot of major modifications. The ending scene is one of them. Forrest Gump is good. Pulp Fiction is good too. But this movie is even better. And I'm glad that I saw it in the theater, not on the videotape.

title: In search of excellence
review:
The Shawshank Redemption never made it to the big screen in Sweden, at least not what I heard of. And I really can't understand why. It is excellent. It's a calm and unsettling story of a man's (Robbins) life in jail, of the friendship between him and his fellow lifer, Red (Freeman) and the disgusting life in a corrupt prison in the 50's and 60's. Excellent performances, great camera angles and one of the very best endings of any film.

Stephen King wrote the story. Why should I be surprised? His novels and short stories make for great films - but most are turned into crap, like It. This one, however, is one of the best movies there is.

title: Forget the rest...
review:
Apologies to all proud Anglophiles, but I have never heard the English language sound so beautiful as during Freeman's narration in the last 20 minutes. Our language has to compete with beautiful languages like Italian, Spanish and French and Darabont's writing really "stepped up to the plate" here.

No clichéd romantic tragedy of unrequited love had to unfold (there was only ONE female speaking role!!!). Only a story of friendship, hope and inner strength was needed to bring tears to the eyes during the final narration.

Unlike many movies of the nineties, this movie gets its strength from fantastic characterisation, great pen-to-paper skills and Deakin's cinematography; words and pictures, not 200 gigabtyes of cyber-FX!

Despite my admiration of James Cameron, this movie beats "Titanic" as well as classics like "Casablanca," "African Queen," "Citizen Kane," "Gone with the Wind," and Hitchcock's "North by Northwest."

title: The "Rocky" of Prison Films
review: This is much more than a prison film.  This is a film about how the human spirit can conquer the most unspeakable abyss and come out clean at the other side.  In addition, the story at the heart of it, of Andy (Tim Robbins) and Red (Morgan Freedman)is simply a story of two men's friendship -- something seldom explored in cinema, and rarely as well.  Lastly, the theme of hope echoes and throughout the film and reverberates in the viewer's minds like an aria against hard prison walls.

title: One of King's, and possibly one of the, best.
review: I read Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption as part of Stephen King's Different Seasons, and loved the story.. to see just how much one person can go through, and not only remain sane, but keep his morals about him, even in the purgatory of a corrupt prison. The book was incredible. But the movie took it one step further, with incredibly well chosen actors and a beautiful sense of the book that is hard to set to a movie, as well as lines that I still remember at the drop of a hat. Incredible, and one of my favorite movies of all time.

title: One of the Best!
review: Hey, I have to say that this movie is one of my favorites.  It is up on my top 10.  Anyway, this movie is amazing.  The story, the acting, and anything else you can think of make this movie a classic.  Morgan Freeman (plays the character red) did an excellent job on his role.  I think he was totally robbed when he didn't get the Oscar for best supporting actor.  To get back on the movie, if you looking for a good one to watch, you have to see this. The movie is wonderfully played.  Also hats off to the great job Tim Robbins did playing his main character Andy Dufresne. If you haven't seen this one, your missing out!!

title: Not just a prison movie but a movie that gives hope
review: After seeing this movie for the first time I was stunned.  Living in Maine i was very interested in the whole story.  The prison featured in the movie is very similar to our own Thomaston State prison.  This is not just a good movie, but a great story as well.  It keeps you wanting to see Andy set free throughout the whole thing.

title: Wow
review: I first saw this movie on TBS one night, and wasn't all that interested in it at first. But as the movie progressed, I found myself totally glued to the TV. This movie is quite possibly the best movie I've ever seen. Every single thing in this movie is perfect, the acting, chemistry, plot. Its all so wonderfully done. The ending of this movie was really great.  Its really hard to describe how good this movie is. Just go get it, you'll never regret seeing it.

title: Fantastic.
review: I'm not going to elaborate on what has already been written by others - except to say that the popularity for this film is enormous.  I don't think I know ANYONE who didn't like it - it will be recognised as one of THE films of the 90's.

title: I hope...
review:
This movie was deeply moving. I have seen it about six times so far and cried the first four times I saw it. As a person who has at times felt as if I was sentenced to "the hole", I could relate to Andy and to Red. Perhaps that is one reason the movie has touched so many people.

The message and heart in this film is profound. When Red said, "I hope....." at the end of the movie, I was hoping too.

title: A Heartfelt Masterpiece
review: OK, so I am a huge fan of Stephen King as well as of the cinema itself, and it took me almost 5 years to finally see The Shawshank Redemption.  I think I was one of the few people on the planet who did not see this fantastic motion picture.  Everything about this film exudes greatness, from the performances of Freeman and Robbins to the masterful screenplay, cinematography, cast and especially the direction.  I agree with most people who fume over the fact that films such as this one (perfect in every sense) rarely, if ever garner an Oscar win.  Its a shame that the big budget over - hyped (and often mediocre at best films) win all the awards while a gem like The Shawshank Redemption comes up empty.  You never grow tired of watching this film and its introspective ending is just perfect.  If you are one of the 4 remaining people who has yet to see this masterpiece, find 2 hours of quiet time and watch it.  You will thank yourself afterwards.

title: It was much better than Cats...
review: What amazes me about the Shawshank Redemption is that I can watch it over and over again without losing interest.  Normally for me, even with movies I enjoy, once is enough.  However, when I'm channel surfing and I flip across Shawshank, I almost always leave it on and watch it to the end.

title: It's just BETTER than other movies...
review:
Okay,...I just watched this film for probably the 20th time, and I could probably watch it a hundred times in a row and not get sick of it. This comment is directed towards anyone who has not seen this film:

GO...

NOW...

I have LITERALLY dragged people off the street and sat them down in front of my television when I've found out that they haven't seen this film.
